name: Dabu mud-resist block printing
summary: Dabu is a Rajasthani hand-block technique in which a paste of mud, lime and natural gum is block-printed onto cloth, dusted with sawdust and sun-dried so that it resists a cold indigo bath; resist-and-dye cycles are repeated to build layered shades. Akola village in Chittorgarh district, home to Chhipa printers on the Beduch river, is widely described as its centre of origin. Recipes vary between centres, and in present-day Akola tar-based resists have partly displaced mud.
